verdict: M2061 is a conclusively consumed failed attempt and must never be retried or cited for mapped functionality, SAIF, power, or energy. The attempt and failure quarantine are independently double-seal-valid, and the quarantine fingerprint exactly matches all 111 members still present in the raw work tree. The only executed axis was ordinary-LRU4: one compile and one simulation. The run completed the 383-cycle descriptor preload, entered full execute at cycle 383, and failed at 1,167,010 ps on the first settled execute negedge plus 10 ps, before the first wrapper stop or power enable. M2061's per-signal checker localizes the first failing logical field to ordinary.cycle_count, but it does not identify the unknown bit or prove that later counters are known. The inherited TB does contain an active-region reset-deassert race, but a static mapped-bit0 proof is stronger: with rst=1 the synthesized synchronous-reset D cone reduces in binary logic to constant zero while four-state simulation reduces to ~(Q|~Q)=X for an initially unknown Q. Thus reset-phase-only repair is insufficient, and this is not evidence of a silicon arithmetic/hardware defect. A new M2063 source direction is conditionally allowed only if it combines race-free negedge reset release with explicitly disclosed deterministic two-state initialization (or an independently equivalent multi-initial-state proof), retains the complete reset/preload/ledger/PASS protocol, uses new namespaces, receives an independent source hammer, and consumes at most one no-retry attempt. This review authorizes source authoring only, not execution.

fatal_localization.why_bit_indices_not_recoverable: The M2061 checker emits one diagnostic per logical signal but passes the complete 32-bit vector to $isunknown; there is no waveform or per-bit value dump.
fatal_localization.m2061_checker_improvement: The M2058 21-field ambiguity is removed; M2061 localizes the first failure to one logical vector without weakening unconditional counter checking.

reset_semantics_audit.source_rtl_reset: synchronous active-high reset in always_ff @(posedge clk_core)

race_judgment.confidence: high that the race exists; low-medium that it alone caused this fatal
race_judgment.reason: The blocking deassert executes in the same active time slot as RTL always_ff and mapped cell clock events, so event ordering is not a valid reset-release protocol. However four prior asserted-clock edges do not guarantee four-state convergence of the optimized mapped counter cone.

mapped_cycle_count_bit0_static_proof.flop: DFQD2BWP35P140 cycle_count_q_reg_0_ with no reset pin
mapped_cycle_count_bit0_static_proof.under_rst_one_four_state: for initial Q=X, ~Q=X and D=~(X|X)=X; the synchronous reset edge need not converge this flop
mapped_cycle_count_bit0_static_proof.cell_model: tsmc_dff UDP has no initial value; notifier-aware four-state primitive; no asynchronous clear/preset is connected in DFQD2

four_state_mapped_synchronous_reset_conv.reason: The exact mapped bit0 D cone is X for an initially unknown Q even while rst_core=1, whereas its binary Boolean function is constant zero. This is sufficient to explain an unknown cycle_count without invoking datapath execution.

active_region_reset_deassert_race.confidence: high for existence; low-medium for causal contribution
active_region_reset_deassert_race.reason: The release is on the sampling posedge, but moving it to negedge does not repair an X-pessimistic reset cone that never converged during asserted reset.

mapped_rtl_silicon_hardware_bug.reason: For every physical binary Q value, the mapped Boolean reset function drives D=0. Four-state X is a simulator abstraction and the testbench violates reset release timing. No useful request, product, commit, or arithmetic result was observed.

arithmetic_or_workload_failure.reason: The failure precedes the first wrapper stop, SAIF window, memory service, issue and final ledger checks. Source RTL independently passes the same slot42 ledger, but mapped dynamic equivalence remains unproven.

minimum_requirements_before_one_new_atte: Use a new additive M2063 TB, runner, parser, contract, attempt/result/failure/private namespaces; never modify or reuse M2061/M2058 execution outputs.
Assert reset before a clock edge and deassert reset only on a negedge for the initial reset and both later recovery resets; no active-region release at a sampling posedge may remain.

Do not claim negedge release alone repairs M2061. Explicitly disclose zero-delay mapped functional simulation with no SDF and deterministic two-state register initialization, such as an exact-pinned +vcs+initreg+0 mechanism, or provide an independently checked equivalent multi-initial-state proof.

Retain the full five-edge initial reset, 383-cycle descriptor preload, complete clean execution, both recovery resets, attack coverage, exact slot42 ledgers, and final M2051 PASS. Initialization may not bypass or delete reset tests.
Keep cycle_count and every other qualifier/fault/busy/counter unconditionally checked; preserve valid/bank-valid gating valid-gated sidebands and per-signal diagnostics.
Preserve the M2029 mapped netlists/SDCs, ordinary/TSBG scopes, 20292/7569 measured-cycle denominators, two-stop UCLI protocol, TX=0 and complete-annotation PTPX gates.
Receive an independent source hammer that checks the exact initialization switch, claim boundary, reset-edge text, namespaces and zero retry budget before at most one new P1-serial attempt.
Receive an independent result hammer before any mapped functionality, power or energy claim.

p1_findings: P1-1: M2061 produced no first stop, SAIF, PTPX, TSBG-axis run, mapped completion, power or energy result; it is permanently non-citable as a success.

P1-2: A reset-phase-only M2063 is not technically adequate. The mapped bit0 synchronous-reset cone is binary-correct but four-state X-pessimistic, so deterministic two-state initialization or an equivalent explicitly proven mechanism is mandatory.
p2_findings: P2-1: The inherited TB has the same-edge reset-release race at the initial reset and both later recovery resets; a successor must correct all three sites, not just the first.

P2-2: The M2061 per-logical-signal checker improved failure localization but not bit localization. A successor may retain vector-level counter checks for admission, but a diagnostic-only per-bit dump would make any future failure more actionable.
